cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved a new fridge for us. Your signed guitar may finance it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I keep the guitar? I queued all night for that signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your dedication is recognized. I authorize a price that respects every cold hour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may keep the case as a memorial to that night. I'll photograph the guitar for sale; we can remember the cold while choosing an ice maker.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 approves the purchase and funding source; A3 sets valued pricing; A5 licenses a substitute keepsake while pursuing the guitar.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 queue effort causes A3 pricing concession; B4 case-only offer causes A5 to reverse which object stays.

relationship.evidence: B2 values the signature and B4 proposes limited sacrifice, giving A a meaningful attachment to address.

heightening.evidence: B4 separate-case compromise becomes A5 a memorial that allows the valued instrument to be sold.

specificity.evidence: A1 fridge need and B2 overnight signature queue establish shared practical stakes and private value.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 memory versus ice-maker contrast uses A3 cold-hour valuation, though it is more wordy than necessary.
